## Introduction

Assessment is one of the most time-critical activities in academic institutions. As class sizes grow and assignments increasingly combine written analysis, source code, diagrams, and screenshots in a single submission, manual grading has become a major bottleneck — leading to delayed feedback, inconsistent scoring, and shallow qualitative comments.

Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) and vision-capable AI models have opened the possibility of automating not just content generation but _evaluation_ — reading a submission and producing a structured, rubric-aligned judgment comparable to a human grader. However, most existing tools handle only a single format: either plain-text essay scoring or unit-test-based code grading. Real assignments are rarely single-format, which motivates a genuinely **multi-modal** evaluation system.

## Problem Statement

Current manual and semi-automated assessment approaches suffer from:

- -   **Grading bottleneck** — faculty handling 60–200+ submissions per cycle cannot give detailed feedback within available time.
    - **Inconsistent scoring** — the same rubric applied by different evaluators (or the same evaluator at different times) shows measurable variance.
    - **Shallow feedback** — time pressure reduces feedback to a single grade with minimal comment.
    - **No multi-modal support** — existing tools evaluate text or code in isolation, ignoring diagrams and mixed-format PDFs.
    - **Delayed turnaround** — students often wait days to weeks, weakening the learning feedback loop.

**Target users:** Students (need fast, specific feedback), Teachers (need reduced workload with retained oversight), Administrators (need visibility into rubric usage and analytics).

## Objectives

![](data:image/png;base64,)

1. Automate assignment evaluation using AI across text, code, and image content.
2. Reduce teachers' manual grading workload while keeping them in the review loop.
3. Generate personalized, evidence-linked feedback rather than generic comments.
4. Evaluate multi-modal submissions (text + code + images) as a single coherent assignment.
5. Improve consistency and fairness in grading through a fixed, weighted rubric.
6. Generate a professional, downloadable PDF evaluation report.

## Proposed System

The proposed system decomposes each submission using a **Document Parser**, routes each content type (text, code, image) to a specialized **AI evaluation engine**, and reconciles their outputs through a **Rubric Mapping Engine** into one 100-point, eight-criterion score with linked feedback — with a mandatory **teacher review** step before results are released to students.

**Key advantages over the existing system:** format-agnostic ingestion (PDF/DOCX/image/code), parallel specialized evaluation per modality, deterministic JSON-schema-based scoring, explainable AI-indicator evidence per criterion, retained human oversight, and a configuration-driven rubric engine for extensibility.

## Key Features

- -   Multi-modal ingestion of assignments in PDF, DOCX, code, and image formats.
    - AI-powered automated evaluation using text, code -capable LLMs.
    - Personalized, evidence-linked feedback for every criterion.
    - Mandatory teacher review and override step before results reach students.
    - Downloadable, professional PDF evaluation reports per assignment.
    - Role-based dashboards for students, teachers, and administrators.
    - Secure, JWT-based authentication and access control.

## Expected Outcomes

- -   A working prototype capable of ingesting mixed-format assignments and producing rubric-aligned, criterion-wise scores with an AI confidence indicator.
    - Reduction in first-pass grading time for a batch of submissions, with teacher effort shifted to review rather than initial scoring.
    - Personalized, evidence-linked feedback delivered within minutes of submission. A downloadable, professional PDF evaluation report per assignment.

## Future Scope

Plagiarism detection via semantic similarity, longitudinal learning analytics, adaptive rubric weighting by course level, voice-based feedback for accessibility, multilingual evaluation support, and offline/on-premise deployment using open-weight models for institutions with data-privacy constraints.
